title: Distributed Rate Limiter & Token Bucket Gateway
problemStatement: Multi-tenant APIs frequently experience 'noisy neighbor' spikes and DDoS vectors that degrade service for all tenants simultaneously. Traditional per-instance rate limiting fails in horizontally-scaled clusters because each node has no global state. Build a low-latency, sliding-window and token-bucket distributed rate limiting proxy that intercepts traffic and coordinates token consumption across a Redis cluster with zero race conditions.
useCases: API Gateways at Razorpay, Swiggy, and Flipkart enforce per-customer rate limits across hundreds of servers. Any company offering a public API (SaaS, fintech, e-commerce) needs this. Directly applicable to Cloudflare, AWS API Gateway, and any microservices ingress layer.
problemItSolves: Without distributed rate limiting, a single abusive client can exhaust shared infrastructure resources, creating cascading failures. This project proves you understand atomic operations, race conditions, and distributed coordination — three topics that appear in every senior backend interview.
recruiterSignal: Shows mastery of Redis advanced patterns (Lua scripts), Go concurrency, and real-world API gateway internals. This exact problem is asked in system design interviews at Razorpay, Meesho, and CRED.
architecture: High-throughput reverse proxy written in Go using atomic Redis Lua scripts to execute sliding window counter increments in < 2ms. Supports gRPC streaming and HTTP middleware headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset). Uses Redis WATCH/MULTI/EXEC for optimistic concurrency.
scaleTargets: Sustain 25,000 req/sec across 4 worker nodes with p99 latency overhead < 3.5ms and 99.99% enforcement accuracy.
verificationRubric: Live deployment or Docker Compose 1-line setup (docker compose up -d)
k6 or Locust benchmark script simulating 25k RPS under concurrent spikes
Redis Lua script preventing check-then-act race conditions under concurrency

title: Multi-Tenant B2B Event Analytics Engine
problemStatement: SaaS telemetry platforms process millions of interaction events daily from web and mobile clients, but querying aggregate funnel conversions, retention cohorts, and time-series metrics on traditional row-oriented OLTP databases results in excessive query latency and timeouts once tables exceed tens of millions of rows. Analytical systems require columnar storage, data compression, and partitioned indexing to scan billions of values per second. This project builds a multi-tenant telemetry ingestion and analytical engine that streams event beacons through Kafka into a partitioned ClickHouse cluster, maintaining sub-second aggregation latencies across multi-million row datasets.
useCases: Product analytics platforms ingest high-throughput user clickstreams to generate real-time behavioral metrics. Neutral architectural reference points include open-source and commercial product analytics systems such as PostHog, Mixpanel, and Amplitude.
problemItSolves: Preventing Part Explosion: ClickHouse creates immutable physical directory parts for every write transaction. Ingesting high-frequency single records directly triggers the 'Too many parts in all data in table' exception. The ingestion pipeline must enforce batch buffering (minimum 10,000 events or 5-second flushes) before persisting to disk.
recruiterSignal: Demonstrates mastery of the OLTP vs. OLAP boundary, columnar database internals (sparse primary keys, column encoding, merge policies), and high-throughput streaming architecture. Directly maps to Data Platform Engineer, Analytics Engineer, and Backend Data Infrastructure roles.
architecture: Node.js/TypeScript HTTP receiver validates incoming JSON beacons against strict schemas and publishes to partitioned Kafka topics keyed by tenant_id. ClickHouse consumes from Kafka via Kafka Engine and buffers columnar batches of 10,000+ records into a ReplacingMergeTree table partitioned by toDate(timestamp) with ZSTD compression. Analytical query layer exposes REST endpoints for funnel conversions, retention cohorts, and time-series metrics.
scaleTargets: Ingestion Throughput: > 10,000 events/sec sustained over 100k test events | Query Latency: p95 < 100ms for 3-step conversion funnel over 10M rows | Storage Compression: Disk compression ratio ≥ [X:1] (target ≥ 6:1) verified via system.parts.
verificationRubric: Environment Health Check: Verify docker compose up -d launches Kafka and ClickHouse with healthy connection status in < 30s.
Ingestion Pipeline Verification: Stream 5,000 synthetic events via npm run seed; verify ClickHouse events table reflects exactly 5,000 rows within 10s.
Funnel Query Execution: Execute npm run query:funnel; verify ClickHouse computes multi-step conversion counts using windowFunnel in < [M ms] (target < 100ms).
Retention Matrix Verification: Execute npm run query:retention; verify query generates 30-day weekly retention cohort matrix matching ground truth.
Storage Compression Verification: Run npm run audit:compression; verify system.parts reports columnar compression ratio ≥ [X:1] (target ≥ 6:1).
portfolioBulletFormula: Architected multi-tenant telemetry ingestion pipeline streaming event beacons through Kafka into ClickHouse; achieved [N] events/sec ingestion throughput and sub-[M ms] aggregate dashboard queries over [K] million events with [X:1] columnar compression.

scaleTargets: Process 5,000 payment requests/sec with < 800ms end-to-end transaction time, 99.99% idempotency guarantee, and daily T+1 settlement batch completing in < 30 minutes.

Double-entry bookkeeping ledger preventing debit without matching credit

portfolioBulletFormula: Built UPI-style payment gateway in Java & Spring Boot; processed 5k transactions/sec with guaranteed idempotency and T+1 settlement batching across simulated multi-bank routing.

title: Service Mesh & mTLS Zero-Trust Microservices Architecture
problemStatement: Microservices architectures have insecure east-west (service-to-service) traffic by default, with no encryption, no service identity, and no traffic management policies. title: Change Data Capture (CDC) & Event Sourcing Pipeline
problemStatement: Microservices need to react to database changes in other services without tight coupling. Traditional polling-based approaches create database load and introduce replication lag. scaleTargets: Propagate database changes to all downstream consumers within 500ms of commit, handle 10,000 change events/sec, and maintain exactly-once delivery guarantees.
verificationRubric: Database INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE replicated to Elasticsearch within 500ms

portfolioBulletFormula: Built CDC pipeline with Debezium and Kafka; propagated PostgreSQL row-level changes to Elasticsearch and 2 downstream consumers within 500ms at 10k events/sec with exactly-once guarantees.

title: Bayesian A/B Experimentation Engine
problemStatement: Fixed-horizon frequentist A/B testing requires accumulating a predetermined sample size before evaluating outcomes, prolonging exposure to suboptimal variants and encouraging premature stopping errors (peeking). The engine enforces minimum statistical power thresholds and computes Expected Loss thresholds rather than relying purely on tail probabilities.

Beta-Binomial conjugate posterior Beta(α + k, β + n - k) evaluated via numerical quadrature or exact closed-form integral for two arms. Expected Loss computed as joint probability integral over loss function. Automated transition to STOPPED_WINNER or STOPPED_INCONCLUSIVE once n ≥ N_min and Expected Loss < ε.
scaleTargets: Ingestion Latency: p99 < 20ms under 10k concurrent synthetic events | Inference Throughput: > 2,000 evaluations/sec on Python 3.11+ | Duration Reduction: Median sample reduction ≥ [X%] vs fixed-sample baseline with empirical false positive rate ≤ [Y%] under A=B null.
